note: Every wait for the wall clock that scripts/check-wall-clock-waits.mjs lets stand, with how many there are in the file and why each is a poll that ends on its condition and not a guess. The list only shrinks.

allowed.reason: Removing a workflow is refused while a job of its own is still finishing; this asks again every half second and gives up after 30 seconds, ending at the first answer that is not "busy".
The two polls every API test shares: they look every 50 ms, end the moment the condition holds and give up at a ceiling that only a hung test reaches.
A poll every 100 ms for a real server process to start answering; it ends the moment the process answers or exits and gives up at its own ceiling.
A poll every 100 ms for a real server process to start answering; it ends the moment the process answers or exits and gives up at its own ceiling.
A poll for a line a real server process has printed, every 25 ms, that ends the moment the line is there and gives up at a ceiling.
The one poll for something a real process has to do, every 10 ms, that ends the moment its condition holds and gives up at a ceiling that only a broken test reaches.
Retry between two /health requests while the published server starts; ends at the first answer and gives up at 30 seconds.

The two waits of the host that drives the VM: five seconds between tries while the VM comes up (15 minutes at most) and twenty seconds between looks at a running phase, which a hang guard of the phase's own timeout ends.
Wait-Until itself: the interval between two runs of its probe, which ends at the first answer and gives up at the caller's hang guard.

The tries between requests and checks in the smoke's own wait loops (server ready, job complete, listen addresses, log line, folder removal, hook processes gone): each ends the moment its condition holds and gives up at a named hang guard.
Retry between two /ready requests while the server starts; ends at the first answer and gives up at 60 seconds.
Five seconds between looks for the workflow run that was just triggered on GitHub, which ends the moment the run is listed.
